report.source_text: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, and CT liver multiphase protocol were obtained and revealed three peripherally enhancing, cystic lesions in the hepatic parenchyma in segments VI (5.4×7.0×4.4 cm), VII (5.1×5.8× 4.2 cm) and VIII (4.3×3.8×4.0 cm) (figure 1). The hepatic vein was nearly completely effaced due to mass effect. CT also demonstrated a large, arterially enhancing, vascular lesion in the porta hepatis measuring up to 3.2 cm which followed blood pool on arterial, portal venous and delayed phases, concerning for a hepatic artery aneurysm (figure 2).

report.source_text: All abscesses decreased in size on repeat liver CTs on HOD 13 and HOD 20, and the hepatic artery aneurysm remained thrombosed. Percutaneous drains were removed due to minimal drainage, and the patient was discharged in good condition on HOD 23 with outpatient intravenous ampicillin until the resolution of undrained liver abscess on imaging. A repeat CT of her liver done at 5 weeks of treatment demonstrated ongoing improvement in abscess size. She was switched to oral amoxicillin with a plan for repeat imaging. The patient remained in good condition without abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Multiple liver abscesses secondary to Listeria monocytogenes complicated by hepatic artery mycotic aneurysm
clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 50s presented with 5 days of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and leukocytosis without fever. Abdominal CT on presentation revealed multiple peripherally enhancing cystic liver lesions consistent with abscesses and a large hepatic artery aneurysm in the porta hepatis. Blood cultures were negative, but hepatic abscess cultures grew Listeria monocytogenes on hospital day 12, confirming the pathogen. Repeat imaging on hospital days 13 and 20 showed decreased abscess size and thrombosis of the hepatic artery aneurysm. Percutaneous drains were removed; the patient was discharged on intravenous ampicillin with continued outpatient treatment and switched to oral amoxicillin with ongoing radiographic improvement and clinical resolution by 5 weeks.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: CT imaging demonstrated multiple peripherally enhancing cystic liver lesions consistent with abscesses in segments VI, VII, and VIII and a hepatic artery aneurysm in the porta hepatis
Hepatic abscess cultures grew Listeria monocytogenes on hospital day 12; blood cultures remained negative

Repeat CT imaging showed decreased abscess size, thrombosis of the hepatic artery aneurysm, removal of percutaneous drains, and clinical improvement leading to discharge and continued outpatient antibiotic treatment with subsequent resolution of symptoms and abscess size
